In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunosuppressive therapies that can enhance the number and/or function of naturally-occurring regulatory T cells.
the role of histone/protein deacylase inhibitors (HDACi), which are a novel class of immunosuppressive drugs, in the treatment of autoimmunity and transplant rejection.
the development and application of novel immunomodulatory therapies for the treatment of human autoimmune and allograft rejection diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HDAC inhibitors are a promising new approach to enhance regulatory T cell function in vivo and that HDAC9 is the most important HDAC for Foxp3 function.

the HDAC inhibitor, valproic acid (VPA), is an immunosuppressant that enhances the generation and suppressive function in vivo of Tregs, and that this effect is dependent on Foxp3 acetyltransferase activity.

the administration of HDACi in vivo enhances Treg function by inducing Foxp3 acetyltransferases and that HDACi therapy may be a useful approach for the treatment of autoimmune diseases and transplantation tolerance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deacetylase inhibition can be used to enhance the generation and function regulatory T cells, thereby allowing the induction of allograft tolerance.
HDACi therapy can promote the generation and function Treg cells, and that this effect can be used to enhance the efficacy of Treg cell-based therapies.
HDAC9 is a critical regulator of Foxp3 function and that HDACi therapy is an effective means of increasing the number and function of regulatory CD4+ T cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HDACi can be used to enhance Foxp3 expression, Treg cell function, and Treg cell-mediated suppression of immune responses.

HDAC inhibitors can be used to promote regulatory T cells (Foxp3+) and their function in vivo, which has important therapeutic implications for the treatment of autoimmune disease and for the induction of transplantation tolerance.
